metaDescription: Seven screwdriver sets compared on handle shape, tip hardness, magnetic tips, Phillips slotted and Torx coverage, ratcheting multibit sets and case design.
expertTake: The Milwaukee 12 piece tri-lobe screwdriver set is our top pick for a handle shape built for grip and torque, plus a comprehensive mix of Phillips and slotted sizes. The Amartisan 10 piece magnetic set is the value pick for a low tier set with magnetic tips and cushion grips. Skip a huge bit driver set if you mostly drive screws in a few sizes, because dedicated handles give better feel and are faster than swapping bits all day.
introParagraphs: A screwdriver set is the tool kit most households use more than any other. The right one matches your fasteners with Phillips, slotted, Torx and hex tips, fits the hand comfortably and keeps its tips sharp enough to avoid camming out and stripping screws.

Handle shape, tip quality and the sizes in the set matter more than total piece count. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for home repair, shop and automotive use, not by the biggest number of pieces.

products.name: Milwaukee 12 piece tri-lobe screwdriver set 4932472003, Phillips and slotted

specList.label: Tips
specList.value: Phillips and slotted in several sizes

products.description:
The Milwaukee set has twelve screwdrivers with tri-lobe handles that spread pressure across the palm. The shape is designed to give more torque with less hand fatigue, and the set covers a range of Phillips and slotted sizes.

A handle you can grip firmly changes how a screwdriver performs, because most stripped screws come from poor pressure and slipping. A twelve piece set contains sizes for most household jobs without extras you do not use. Against the CRAFTSMAN bi material sets, the Milwaukee has a more refined handle. Against the DEWALT MAXFIT set, it has more pieces.

Wipe tips and handles after use and keep the set together in a roll or drawer. Replace worn tips, which cam out and damage screws. Owners often say a firm grip is the secret to not stripping screws, and a handle that fills the palm lets you press down and turn without twisting your wrist.
products.bestFor: Daily household and trade use where grip comfort matters.
pros: Tri-lobe handle spreads pressure for comfort and torque
Twelve piece range covers common Phillips and slotted sizes
Good value for the number of useful pieces
cons: No Torx or hex bits in this set
Upper mid price tier
Only handles, with no ratcheting option

products.name: DEWALT MAXFIT combination screwdriver set DWHT65102, 8 piece
products.description:
The DEWALT MAXFIT set has eight screwdrivers in combination Phillips and slotted sizes. It is a compact kit for everyday household repairs and a staple of a home toolbox.

A smaller set with the right sizes covers most screws you meet, and the MAXFIT range is DEWALT's value line of hand tools. The handles are comfortable and the tips are made to fit snugly. Against the Milwaukee, it has fewer pieces and a lower price tier. Against the CRAFTSMAN 12 piece set, it has a stronger brand name for professional tools.

Store the set together and wipe tips. Replace any that cam out regularly. A compact eight piece set also fits easily in a kitchen drawer, which is where most household screwdrivers get used.
products.bestFor: Everyday household repairs in a compact set.
pros: Eight pieces cover common household sizes
cons: No Torx or hex tips
Fewer sizes than the 12 piece sets
Less specialised than a magnetic precision set

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 12 piece bi-material screwdriver set CMHT65071N
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN 12 piece set has bi-material handles that combine a hard core with a softer grip, in Phillips and slotted sizes. It is a straightforward home toolbox set at a lower tier than the pro brands.

A softer grip on a hard handle gives comfort without losing torque, and twelve pieces cover most household jobs. The set lacks the shaped handle of the Milwaukee, and the steel is not marketed as premium. Against the Milwaukee, it costs less. Against the CRAFTSMAN 8 piece bi-material set, it has more sizes.

Wipe tips and keep the set organised in a drawer or roll. Replace tips that wear. If you only own one set at home, this is a sensible all rounder that you will not worry about losing.
products.bestFor: General home use at a low tier.
pros: Bi-material handles balance grip and torque
Low price tier from a known brand
cons: No Torx or hex tips
Handles are less shaped than premium sets
Tip quality is standard, not premium

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 42 piece screwdriver set CMHT65300, Phillips, slotted, Torx, acetate handle
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN 42 piece set includes Phillips, slotted and Torx screwdrivers with acetate handles. It is a wide range for a workshop that deals with different fastener types, from furniture to electronics.

Torx tips matter because many appliances, cars and electronics use them. Acetate handles are classic, tough and resistant to many chemicals, though they are less cushioned than soft grip handles. Against the 12 piece sets, it covers far more types. Against the Amartisan 43 piece set, it has a more traditional style and brand name.

Keep the set organised, wipe tips and replace damaged ones. The wider range makes it a good companion to a socket set, since many bolts and screws overlap in cars and appliances.
products.bestFor: Workshops with mixed fasteners such as Torx and Phillips.
pros: 42 pieces cover Phillips, slotted and Torx
Acetate handles are tough and chemical resistant
Wide range for appliances and cars
cons: Many small tips are easy to misplace
Acetate is less cushioned than soft grips
Mid price tier

products.name: CRAFTSMAN ratcheting screwdriver multibit set CMHT68001, 26 piece
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN ratcheting set has a ratcheting handle and a selection of interchangeable bits, 26 pieces in total. A ratchet lets you turn a screw without lifting and regripping the handle, which speeds up repetitive work.

Bit driver sets are compact and cover many tip types, though a single handle feels less refined than dedicated drivers and bits can wobble in the chuck. Against the dedicated handle sets, it is faster but less precise. Against the Amartisan sets, it is a ratchet rather than fixed handles.

Keep the bits in their case and check the ratchet for dirt. Replace worn bits. Because the handle also stores bits, it works as a grab and go tool for jobs around the house and in the car.
pros: Ratcheting action speeds up repetitive driving
cons: Bits can wobble in the chuck
Less feel than dedicated screwdrivers
Ratchet mechanism is a wear point

products.name: Amartisan 10 piece magnetic screwdriver set, 5 Phillips and 5 slotted tips, cushion grips
products.description:
The Amartisan 10 piece set has five Phillips and five slotted screwdrivers with magnetic tips and cushion grips. Magnetic tips hold a screw on the end, which helps in awkward spots where you cannot hold the screw by hand.

A cushion grip is comfortable, and the low price tier makes it a sensible set to keep in a drawer or car. The brand is less established than CRAFTSMAN or Milwaukee, and tip hardness is not documented as precisely. Against the Amartisan 43 piece set, it has fewer pieces. Against the CRAFTSMAN 12 piece set, it has magnetic tips.

Keep the tips clean and replace any that wear. Wipe the handles. Many owners keep a set like this in a car or a drawer for quick jobs where the premium set stays at home.
products.bestFor: Light household use and a budget toolbox.
pros: Magnetic tips hold screws in tight spots
Five Phillips and five slotted sizes
cons: No Torx or hex tips
Brand has less track record
Tip hardness is not specified

products.name: Amartisan 43 piece magnetic screwdriver set with case, slotted, Phillips, hex, Pozidriv, Torx

specList.label: Tips
specList.value: Slotted, Phillips, hex, Pozidriv and Torx

products.description:
The Amartisan 43 piece set includes slotted, Phillips, hex, Pozidriv and Torx tips with magnetic tips and a case. It is a broad set at a low tier, covering most fastener types around a home.

Pozidriv is a Phillips like drive common on European furniture and screws, and mistaking it for Phillips can strip heads. Having both helps. Against the CRAFTSMAN 42 piece set, the Amartisan has magnetic tips and a lower price tier, and the CRAFTSMAN has a more established name. Against the 10 piece Amartisan set, it covers far more tip types.

Return tips to their slots after use. Check the case latches and replace worn tips. The case keeps the many small tips tidy, which is the main practical advantage of a bigger set.
products.bestFor: Broad fastener coverage on a budget.
pros: 43 pieces cover slotted, Phillips, hex, Pozidriv and Torx
cons: Brand has less pro track record
Tip hardness is not specified
Many small pieces to keep track of

buyingCriteria.explanation: Phillips and slotted cover most household screws, Torx is common on appliances, cars and electronics and Pozidriv appears on European furniture. A set should include the sizes you use, usually Phillips 1, 2 and 3 and slotted from small to large. Using the wrong tip strips screws. The usual buyer mistake is buying on piece count and finding the three sizes you use most are only available as awkward bits.

A handle that fits your hand gives more torque with less effort. Tri-lobe designs, as on the Milwaukee, bi-material grips, as on the CRAFTSMAN and cushion grips, as on the Amartisan, aim to reduce slipping. Acetate handles are tough but less cushioned. Test the handle in your hand if you can, since a shape that suits one person can feel wrong to another.

A tip that fits snugly in the screw head cams out less. Better sets use hardened steel and precise tip shapes. Worn tips round off and are the main cause of stripped screws, so replace them when they wear. Check the tip length, because short stubby drivers reach tight spots and long ones reach deep recesses.

A magnetic tip holds a screw on the end of the driver, useful when working overhead or in a tight space. The Amartisan sets have magnetic tips. Magnets can pick up filings and are unsuitable near some electronics. Look for tips that are ground to a precise shape, as a rough tip grips poorly and wears fast.

Dedicated screwdrivers give better feel and torque, while ratcheting multibit drivers like the CRAFTSMAN 26 piece set are fast and compact. Use fixed handles for precision and ratcheting bits for speed. If you work on electronics, add a precision set with small tips, since a normal set cannot handle tiny screws.

A bigger set covers more fasteners but has more small pieces to lose. A twelve piece set often covers most needs. Cases, rolls and holders keep tips organised, and a messy set is a frustrating set. Consider buying a quality Phillips 2, the most used size, as a standalone driver if your set's version feels weak.

specDecoder.meaning: Both have a cross shaped head, but Pozidriv has extra small ribs and needs a matching driver. Using Phillips on Pozidriv strips the screw.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Amartisan 43 piece set includes both.

specDecoder.meaning: A six lobed star drive that resists cam out. It is common on cars, appliances and electronics.
specDecoder.watchFor: The CRAFTSMAN 42 piece and Amartisan 43 piece sets include Torx.

specDecoder.meaning: A handle with a hard core and a soft outer grip. It balances torque and comfort.
specDecoder.watchFor: The CRAFTSMAN 12 piece set uses it.

specDecoder.meaning: A handle shape with three lobes that fit the palm. It spreads pressure and improves grip.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Milwaukee uses it, and the shape is a comfort feature, not a strength rating.

specDecoder.meaning: A tip that holds a ferrous screw. It prevents dropping screws in tight spots.
specDecoder.watchFor: Magnets can pick up filings and can affect delicate electronics.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tip coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sets from 8 to 43 pieces and which tip types and sizes they include. We favoured useful coverage over raw count. We did not drive screws with any of them. Owner feedback patterns about tip wear, magnet strength and handle comfort shaped our scoring.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handle design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tri-lobe, bi-material, cushion and acetate handles. Comfortable, secure grips scored higher. We compared handle styles across all seven sets and noted which suit different hand sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tip quality signals
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed magnetic tips and any steel details in the listings. Where the listing was vague we assumed ordinary quality. Where a listing did not give details of the steel we assumed ordinary quality.

howWeEvaluated.title: Set format
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered fixed handle sets against ratcheting bit sets and noted storage. Organised storage scored higher. We checked whether sets include the sizes that cover most household screws.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed brand support, tip wear and owner feedback patterns about stripped screws. Established brands scored higher. Storage solutions were weighed because lost tips are a frequent complaint.

cards.label: Fixed handles
cards.text: The Milwaukee, DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN sets give better feel and torque for each size.

cards.label: Ratcheting bits
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN 26 piece set is fast and compact. It gives up some feel and bits can wobble.

howToChoose.note: Choose fixed handles for precision and ratcheting bits for speed.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Phillips 1, 2 and 3, a few slotted sizes and a comfortable grip. A magnetic tip helps with dropped screws.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Milwaukee and CRAFTSMAN 12 piece sets cover home repair, and the Amartisan sets add magnets.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use screwdrivers daily or want comfort and brand support. The Milwaukee set fits.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use them occasionally. The Amartisan or CRAFTSMAN 12 piece sets are enough.

maintenance.why: Oil and dirt make grips slippery and tips slip. Wipe them dry. Hang drivers on a magnetic strip so tips are visible.
Rounded tips cam out and strip screws. Replace or retire them. Rub a drop of oil on the shank every few months.
Lost tips mean a wrong size gets used. Return each to its slot. Check handles for cracks.
Magnets pick up metal filings. Wipe the tips with a rag. Keep bits in their holder so sizes do not mix.
Moisture rusts tips. Keep the set in a drawer or case. Dry tools after working outdoors.

faq.q: How many screwdrivers do I need?
faq.a: For most homes, Phillips 1, 2 and 3 and two or three slotted sizes cover almost everything. A 12 piece set is plenty. Many owners say a quality Phillips 2 screwdriver gets more use than the rest of a set put together.

They look similar but are not interchangeable. Using Phillips on Pozidriv strips screws, so buy both if you work on European furniture. Press firmly into the screw head and turn slowly, which reduces the chance of cam out.
They help hold screws in tight spots. Avoid them near delicate electronics and clean filings regularly. Do not use a screwdriver as a pry bar or chisel, since this damages the tip.

Fixed handles give better feel and torque, and ratcheting bit drivers are faster for repetitive work. Many people keep both. If a screw is stuck, a drop of penetrating oil and a firm push usually works better than extra force.
Usually a worn or wrong size tip, or not pressing down enough. Match the tip to the screw and push firmly. Keep a spare set in the car for roadside repairs and quick fixes.
Yes if you work on cars, appliances or electronics, where Torx is common. Include a set of tips up to T30. Wear safety glasses when you drive screws overhead or into hard material.
